summary: The initial screen mismatch at step 1523 came from pray.c:pleased() reading the game-level wielded-object slot incorrectly in JS: C uses global uwep, represented by state.uwep, while the old JS branch looked at u.uwep and skipped the pat-on-the-head weapon reward. After correcting that mapping, the same admitted play reached the genuine pleased() action-7/8 crown branch at step 1746; implementing pray.c:gcrownu() then made the complete 1818-step segment match.

source.branch: pleased() no-trouble high-alignment pat-on-the-head weapon reward, followed later by action 7/8 with PIOUS-or-better alignment record and no previous Hand of Elbereth crown
dependencies: The weapon reward reads the game-level C uwep global, represented by state.uwep in JavaScript; u.uwep is not the C owner.
gcrownu() reuses the existing JS source owners for deity messages, object creation and naming, blessing, dropping, artifact discovery, inventory refresh, and weapon-skill updates.
callers: js/cmd.js dispatches #pray to js/pray.js:dopray(); pray.c:prayer_done() invokes pleased() after a successful prayer.
pray.c:pleased() invokes gcrownu() for action 7/8 when alignment record is at least PIOUS and the hero has not already received a Hand of Elbereth.

relevantSource.caller: pray.c:pleased() lines 1071-1381. At the initial mismatch, no trouble and high alignment set pat_on_head; the recorded rn2(9)=1 selects the weapon reward in case 1.
relevantSource.helper: pray.c:gcrownu() lines 805-996 grants the alignment-specific Hand of Elbereth, messages or spellbook/artifact gift, eligible weapon enhancement, inventory refresh, and an extra weapon-skill credit.
relevantSource.js: js/pray.js:pleased() now uses state.uwep for the pat-on-the-head weapon reward and calls the ported gcrownu() from the eligible case 7/8 branch.

evidence: The admitted baseline is unchanged: recording SHA b7110997075e6b608967a17e7700f6859da935e09183c98662928935ff0bbd2c, with 1809/1818 screens, 61686/61695 RNG calls, and 1814/1818 cursors matched.

The first mismatch at segment 0, step 1523 is a screen and cursor boundary: C displays the --More-- prompt before the pat-on-the-head weapon message; the original JS used u.uwep, which was undefined, so it skipped the wielded-weapon reward.

The initial crown explanation at step 1523 was counter-evidence, not the cause: the recorded rn2(9)=1 belongs to pleased() pat_on_head, and C action 7/8 plus gcrownu() is reached later. Once the wielded-slot read was corrected, replay advanced to a new first mismatch at step 1746 with the actual unported gcrownu() marker.

After porting gcrownu() and correcting pleased() to state.uwep, bounded replay run-FnXgIQ matched all 1818 recorded steps, including screens, cursors, RNG calls, and input boundary; it reported no refusal or unported markers. The admitted recording and recipe were not changed.
Focused prayer tests passed 68/68 in bounded run-pOUUc5; npm run lint passed in bounded run-8WPejo.
